title: Rituals We No Longer Explain
sentences: My family performs a number of small rituals at the end of the year.
Nobody can now explain where most of them came from.
One of them involves a chair that has to remain empty during dinner.
As a child I assumed every household did something similar.
When I asked my grandmother, she said her mother had started it.
The reason had apparently not survived even one generation.
We continue anyway, with something between affection and embarrassment.
An outsider would find the whole performance faintly absurd.
What the ritual preserves is not its meaning but its repetition.
That may be the only thing a family reliably manages to pass on.
